subject: Cloud Computing
title: Market Share: Who Leads and Why
description: Learn Market Share: Who Leads and Why in one minute.

hook.text: AWS: 31%. Azure: 24%. Google Cloud: 11%. Everyone else: 34%. Those four numbers define cloud computing.

buildup.text: AWS leads in total revenue. Azure is closing the gap fastest. Google leads in specific niches.

discovery.text: The 'everyone else' category includes Alibaba, Oracle, IBM, and hundreds of regional providers.

twist.text: Market share barely shifts year-to-year. Cloud is sticky — once you're on a platform, you tend to stay.

climax.text: The cloud market is still growing at 20%+ per year. Even losing share means growing in absolute revenue.

punchline.text: In cloud, even third place is a multi-billion-dollar business.

quiz.question: Why does cloud market share rarely shift dramatically year-to-year?
options: Cloud platforms are sticky — migration costs keep customers in place
Government regulations prevent companies from switching providers
All cloud providers offer identical services at identical prices

details.summary: AWS leads the cloud infrastructure market with roughly 31% share, followed by Azure at around 25% and Google Cloud at about 11%. The remaining third is split among dozens of providers. Market share has shifted as Azure gains enterprise customers and Google Cloud grows with AI workloads.
details.whyItMatters: Market share reflects where the industry is investing and which providers have the most operational experience. Leaders benefit from economies of scale that drive down costs for all customers.
takeaways: AWS holds roughly 31% of the cloud infrastructure market
Azure has grown to approximately 25% share
Google Cloud holds about 11% and is growing with AI demand

faq.question: Why is AWS still the market leader?
faq.answer: AWS had a five-year head start, launching in 2006 before serious competition. This enabled them to build the broadest service catalog, largest partner ecosystem, and deepest operational expertise. Many of the world's largest companies built on AWS early and face high switching costs.

faq.question: Is Azure catching up to AWS?
faq.answer: Azure's market share has grown steadily, driven by enterprise customers migrating from Microsoft on-premises products. Microsoft's bundling of Azure with enterprise agreements and Office 365 gives it a strong sales advantage. However, AWS maintains a significant lead in total revenue.
